definitions.WORKS: survived out-of-sample WITH a noise floor run AND funded risk measured — all three
definitions.NEEDS MORE WORK: promising but under-evidenced; the exact sample or data that would settle it is stated
definitions.DEAD: tested and failed; do not retest

rows.name: News filter (pre-open high-impact blackout)
rows.tested: Veto any NY pre-market entry that would be open going into a pre-open high-impact release. Not fitted — the calendar is published in advance, so it is knowable at fill by construction.
rows.numbers: +$2,984.75 sized on the working baseline; day-clustered 95% CI [+$894, +$4,970]; p=0.005. Kill test: the largest avoided trade is a WINNER (+$537) so removing it makes the delta larger (+$3,521.75); 0 of 23 single removals flip the sign. Calendar-shift placebo: real +$2,392.75 beats ALL TEN shifted calendars, which are mostly negative.
rows.noise_floor: Calendar-shift placebo, 10 shifts (±1..5 trading days). Real beats all ten. p=0.091 — the 1/11 floor, which cannot reach 0.05 by construction.
rows.funded: Naked bust 0.98% → 0.42%; max drawdown $1,721 → $1,569; min available DD $1,572 → $1,780; daily-limit breach days 0 → 0; 0.00% with the full spine.
rows.caveats: Decomposition: 92% of the benefit is avoided-trade P&L, 14% resizing, −6% new trades. CPI/PPI/NFP veto NOTHING (34 blackout days, 0 avoided trades). 8 of 9 release types rest on one or two trades. The second arm is a sensitivity check, not a replication (83% shared trades, same largest avoided trade, CI spans zero).

rows.name: Give-back gap by segment (early vs late)
rows.tested: Pre-registered: does conditional give-back — P(finished red | reached +1R) — differ by pre-market segment beyond chance? Fixed segments, no re-bucketing.
rows.numbers: 32.4% early / 27.6% mid / 11.1% late. Primary statistic early−late = +21.2 percentage points. Day-clustered 95% CI [+2.0pp, +38.1pp], bootstrap p=0.034.
rows.noise_floor: 2,000-draw day-block permutation of outcome labels: p=0.0850. Registered rule required p<0.05 AND a CI excluding zero — it got one of two.
rows.funded: Not measured — it is a descriptive asymmetry, not yet a rule, so there is nothing to size.
rows.caveats: Reported INCONCLUSIVE exactly as the registration required, not reinterpreted as a near-miss.
rows.settle: The late segment is the binding constraint: it needs ~28 +1R-reaching trades and has 18, a shortfall of 10. At the observed rate (0.124 such trades per trading day) that is ~80 further trading days, roughly 4 months, of live or shadow data.

rows.name: N-minute timer exit (45 min)
rows.tested: Hold with the original stop live; if not stopped, close at market at the close of bar N. No trailing at any point.
rows.numbers: PM P&L +$29,598 at 45m vs canon +$21,098. Grid: +$21,485 / +$29,598 / +$29,026 / +$17,630 at 30/45/60/90 — a hump, NOT a plateau, falling BELOW canon at 90m; spread is 49% of the level. Money is concentrated: 2026 +$7,693 of +$8,500; OOS +$9,075 vs IS −$575; late segment +$5,736 on 29 trades.
rows.noise_floor: None that can validate it. It was found POST-HOC after the pre-registered select-on-IS procedure rejected it, and 15 of 68 sweep configurations flip negative-to-positive by chance.
rows.funded: Measured, and it is worse: naked bust 0.40% → 2.02% at 45m (5×) and 10.66% at 90m (27×); max drawdown $1,569 → $1,637 (45m) and $2,441 (90m); daily-limit breach days 0 → 1 (45m) and 2 (90m). Takes a full 1R on 55% of trades with no trailing. 0.00% with the full spine.
rows.caveats: Raises expectancy AND raises bust probability — on the stated rule that combination is worse, not better, on the naked account.
rows.settle: Forward evidence only. The Part-4 shadow harness logs it in parallel every session; the forward-only slice is currently EMPTY. Nothing in the existing book can confirm it because the regime boundary is in the wrong place and there is only one of them.

rows.name: H1 — flat R targets (1.5R–4R)
rows.tested: Replace the canon's management with a fixed R target, walk-forward, funded sizing.
rows.numbers: Every target loses to canon out-of-sample. Best cell (4R) $11,771 vs incumbent $15,670; bust 23.04% vs 2.92%; drop-5 worse in every cell. Re-confirmed on the current book: target 1.0R −$12,974 OOS, 2.0R −$8,825, 4.0R −$3,826.
rows.noise_floor: Walk-forward, expanding monthly — picked 4R every month and still lost.
rows.caveats: This reverses the earlier leaky-book RR sweep, which is on the dead-numbers list.

rows.name: H4 — bar-close MAE cuts (0.6R–0.9R)
rows.tested: Exit at the first bar close whose adverse excursion exceeds θ·R, strictly before the canon exit bar.
rows.numbers: Registered falsifier fired exactly as predicted: winner close-MAE max is 0.704R in-sample but 0.912R out-of-sample, so every θ cuts at least one winner. Best cell $17,090 < incumbent $18,376; drop-5 also worse.

rows.name: H2 — day-type bias gate (skip against bias)
rows.tested: Skip trades taken against the day-type bias derived from the committed volume-profile artefact.
rows.numbers: Raises mean R (+0.523 vs +0.370) but LOSES funded dollars in BOTH halves: 2025 $2,593 vs $3,691; 2026 $14,427 vs $14,685. A composition effect, not a gate.
rows.noise_floor: Alignment counts verified against the independent lane (no_bias 105 / with 61 / against 50).
rows.funded: Yes — it is the funded-dollar result that kills it.
rows.caveats: Mean R improving while dollars fall is the signature of dropping small winners.

rows.name: Breakeven stop moved at +1R
rows.tested: Move the stop to entry once +1R is touched; frictionless, active from the bar after the touch.
rows.numbers: 59 of 108 IS trades touch +1R; 27 would be stopped at breakeven. Their actual outcomes sum to +$1,139.75 (mean R +0.014) — 20 losses saved (−$3,110) against 7 winners forgone (+$4,249), including one +4R reacher.
rows.noise_floor: Not required — the effect is a wash before any inference.
rows.funded: Not needed; a wash at 1 lot cannot improve funded dollars.

rows.name: 68-configuration exit/management sweep
rows.tested: 17 management rules × 4 time-of-day scopes, selected on the in-sample half and judged out-of-sample.
rows.numbers: IS-selected rule (target 4.0R, all trades) gained +$4,273 in-sample and lost −$3,826 out-of-sample. Only 18 of 68 beat canon OOS — fewer than a coin flip.
rows.noise_floor: Best-of-68 selection null over 500 day-block-permuted splits: picking the best of 68 on ANY random half yields a median +$6,006 IS by construction (the real +$4,273 is BELOW that, 21st percentile) and shrinks to a median −$1,045 OOS. Real OOS sits at the 21st percentile against a >95th gate.
rows.funded: Not reached — the selection failed first.
rows.caveats: Median in-sample-to-out-of-sample shrinkage is −$7,050. That is the measured price of sweeping on this book.

rows.name: Q1 — entry order flow (11 features)
rows.tested: Does strictly pre-fill entry order flow separate the trades that pay? The honest re-test of conf_PM, which was itself an order-flow entry-conviction signal and was the leak.
rows.numbers: Best out-of-sample |ρ| = 0.093. NO feature survives family-wise correction (M_eff 8.00 of 11 nominal, per-test α 0.0064). Every tercile-transfer CI spans zero.
rows.noise_floor: Day-block permutation plus family-wise Šidák on the effective test count.
rows.funded: Not reached — no rule was produced to size.
rows.caveats: Direction-blind falsifier is effectively a tie: signed 0.0934 vs blind 0.0912, a margin of 0.0022.

rows.name: Q2 — order flow beyond gap size
rows.tested: Does entry order flow add anything once |gap| — knowable at 08:00 with no tape at all — is already known?
rows.numbers: |gap| alone carries ρ +0.153 (p=0.036), LARGER than every order-flow feature tested. After rank-residualising on |gap|, NO feature survives family-wise correction.
rows.noise_floor: Day-clustered bootstrap plus family-wise correction on M_eff.
rows.caveats: The gap finding itself is registered separately (Amendment 5) and is non-monotone across terciles — that is a different, still-open question.

rows.name: In-trade order flow at a retrace (exit-side)
rows.tested: Pre-registered before scoring: at a 0.5R give-back from a +1R peak, does in-trade order flow distinguish a retrace that RESUMES from one that REVERSES?
rows.numbers: Every out-of-sample AUC sits on 0.5 (0.464–0.551); none survives. Base rate: 85% of retraces resume (60.2% when restricted to bars at or before the canon's own exit — the tradeable figure).
rows.noise_floor: Per-bar shift tests pass 20/20 buckets; trade-clustered bootstrap intervals.
rows.caveats: Underpowered below |AUC−0.5| = 0.147 with only 17 reversals in the whole sample — absence of a result is not evidence of absence of an effect.

rows.name: Confluence composite (13 features, ridge, daily walk-forward)
rows.tested: Rank-normalised weighted composite, weights by ridge against realised R, penalty chosen inside each fold, expanding-window daily refit.
rows.numbers: Real ρ +0.0645 over 142 out-of-sample predictions. Sits at the 92.70th percentile of 2,000 day-block-shuffled runs against a registered >99th-percentile gate.
rows.noise_floor: 2,000 shuffles of the identical end-to-end pipeline. p99 = +0.1453.
rows.funded: Conviction sizing part 2 was GATED on the composite clearing the floor and was correctly NOT RUN.
rows.caveats: Falsifier (b) fires — the composite loses to its own best component, cvd_15 at +0.0658. Falsifier (c) fires — random weights on the same pool reach p95 +0.1374, and the fitted composite sits at only the 74.6th percentile of random draws.

dead_numbers.why: Computed on the SUPERSEDED LEAKY book at 1 lot in R-space. Re-run on a remediated book with funded sizing and walk-forward, every fixed target 1.5R–4R loses to the canon's own management. Never quote it as a live result.
That is a WHOLE-BOOK MECHANICAL figure. The pre-market portion is about $17k mechanical and about $3k sized. Quoting $23k as a pre-market or funded number overstates it several times over.
Counts resumes anywhere in trade life, including after the canon had already closed the position. The TRADEABLE figure is 60.2%. Use that one.
Different windows. The certified book starts 2025-06-02; the working baseline starts 2025-07-01. The like-for-like comparison is +$18,113 → +$21,098, and the difference is the news filter alone.

dead_numbers.n: “The leaky arm independently replicates the news filter”
dead_numbers.why: It does not. The two arms share 83% of trades, veto the same days, and have the SAME largest avoided trade. The leaky arm's CI [−$294, +$3,925] spans zero. It is a sensitivity check.
